column3: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those who are not strong, and not to please ourselves.
Let each of us please the neighbor for what is good, toward building up.
For even Christ did not please himself, but just as it is written, “The insults of those insulting you fell on me.”
For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
Now may the God of endurance and encouragement give you the same mind toward one another according to Christ Jesus,
so that with one accord, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore receive one another, just as Christ also received you, for the glory of God.
For I say that Christ became a servant of the circumcised on behalf of the truth of God, to confirm the promises to the fathers,
and for the Gentiles to glorify God for mercy, just as it is written, “For this reason I will confess you among the Gentiles, and I will sing praise to your name.”
And again he says, “Rejoice, Gentiles, with his people.”
And again, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples praise him.”
And again Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, and the one who rises to rule Gentiles; in him Gentiles will hope.”
Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
And I myself am convinced concerning you, my brothers and sisters, that you yourselves also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
But I wrote to you more boldly in part, as reminding you again, because of the grace given to me by God
to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, serving as a priest of the good news of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
Therefore I have reason for boasting in Christ Jesus in the things relating to God.
For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ accomplished through me for the obedience of Gentiles, by word and deed,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the good news of Christ.
And in this way I make it my ambition to announce the good news not where Christ was named, so that I might not build on another’s foundation,
but just as it is written, “Those to whom nothing was announced concerning him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
Therefore I also was hindered many times from coming to you.
But now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having had a longing for many years to come to you,
whenever I go to Spain—for I hope while passing through to see you and to be sent forward there by you, once I have first enjoyed your company in part—
but now I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
For they were pleased, and indeed they are debtors to them. For if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual things, they also owe it to serve them in material things.
Therefore, when I have completed this and sealed this fruit to them, I will depart through you for Spain.
And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in prayers to God on my behalf,
so that I may be rescued from those who disobey in Judea and that my service for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
so that by the will of God I may come to you with joy and be refreshed together with you.
Now may the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
